title: Prawn Pad Thai
subtitle: Thai stir-fried rice noodles with prawns, egg, and tamarind sauce
excerpt: Pad Thai is Thailand's most famous noodle dish: a fast wok stir-fry of rice noodles with a sour-sweet tamarind sauce, crunchy peanuts, and fresh lime. Green beans stand in for bean sprouts here.
sourceNotes: Pad Thai was promoted as a national dish by the Thai government in the 1940s. The tamarind-fish sauce combination is the defining flavour of the dish.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Make the sauce up to a week ahead and store in the fridge. Soak the noodles up to 1 hour before cooking.

content.text: Cook this in batches rather than all at once. One large portion of pad Thai at home needs a restaurant-size burner. Split it into two or three smaller stir-fries and combine in the serving bowl.

items.prepNote: flat rice noodles, soaked in cold water 30 minutes and drained

content.text: Mix the fish sauce, tamarind paste, and palm sugar in a bowl. Stir until the sugar dissolves. Taste: it should be sour, salty, and slightly sweet in equal measure.
Blanch the green beans in boiling water for 2 minutes. Drain and set aside.
Heat the wok over the highest heat until smoking. Add 2 tablespoons of oil. Stir-fry the prawns for 2 minutes until just pink. Remove and set aside.
Add the remaining oil and garlic. Fry for 20 seconds. Add the noodles and pour in the sauce. Toss for 1 minute.
Push the noodles to the side of the wok. Pour the beaten eggs into the empty space. Scramble for 1 minute, then fold through the noodles.
Add the prawns, green beans, and half the spring onion. Toss everything together for 1 minute more.
Serve immediately, topped with peanuts, the remaining spring onion, coriander, and lime wedges on the side.

items.symptom: The noodles are clumping and sticking to the wok.
items.cause: The wok was not hot enough or the noodles were over-soaked.
items.fix: Add a tablespoon of water and toss quickly with tongs.

items.cause: The tamarind was strong or too much was used.
items.fix: Balance with more palm sugar or a splash of fish sauce.

items.cause: They were cooked too long in the initial stir-fry and again at the end.
items.fix: Cook prawns 90 seconds first; they only need 30 seconds at the end.
